# Results — Study 356 (the GLP-1 / Ozempic basket)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The "Ozempic trade" — buy
**LLY + NVO** (a 50/50 weight-loss-drug basket) to ride the GLP-1 boom — tested against the
market (**SPY**) and the healthcare sector (**XLV**). Adjusted-close (total-return) daily
prices from Yahoo Finance. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | Yahoo Finance via `yfinance`, **adjusted close** (total return — dividends reinvested) |
| Tickers | LLY, **NVO (US ADR)**, XLV (Health Care SPDR), SPY |
| Window | **2018-01-02 → 2026-06-18** (2,126 daily returns) · as-of pull 2026-06-21 |
| Basket | 50/50 LLY/NVO, daily-rebalanced (fixed weight) |
| NVO note | peaked **$137.4** (2024-06-25), last **$43.2** — **−69% from peak** |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — a single ~8.5-year window dominated by
> one product cycle; the "alpha" is **not survivorship-clean in spirit**: LLY and NVO are
> picked *because* they won the GLP-1 race (recency / post-hoc selection), which biases the
> excess **upward**. *Tradability* — this is a **two-name** bet (corr LLY–NVO only 0.40), so
> the basket's headline is mostly the path of one stock.

## Headline performance (total return, rf = 0)

| series | CAGR | vol | Sharpe | total | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| LLY | 36.9% | 31.8% | 1.16 | 1,366.8% | −34.5% |
| NVO | 13.5% | 33.5% | 0.40 | 93.0% | **−74.7%** |
| **basket 50/50** | **25.2%** | 27.4% | **0.92** | 510.7% | **−49.3%** |
| XLV | 10.1% | 17.4% | 0.58 | 105.4% | −28.4% |
| SPY | 15.5% | 19.2% | 0.81 | 216.5% | −33.7% |

The basket *does* beat both benchmarks on raw return and Sharpe. The question is whether the
**excess** is real, or one stock and a story.

## Signal — the excess is WEAK (HAC inference)

Mean **excess** return vs each benchmark, with a Newey-West (HAC) *t* (lag 7). The bar for
`REAL` is **HAC-t ≥ 2**.

| test | ann excess / alpha | HAC-t | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| basket − SPY (mean excess) | +9.68% | **1.10** | fails the bar |
| basket − XLV (mean excess) | +15.14% | **2.01** | borderline |
| market-model α, basket ~ SPY | +15.18%/yr | **1.78** (β=0.65) | fails the bar |
| market-model α, basket ~ XLV | +15.45%/yr | **2.05** (β=0.97) | borderline |

Block-bootstrap (21-day blocks, 5,000 reps) of the basket−XLV excess: **+15.1%/yr**, 95% CI
**[+0.2%, +29.3%]**, P(>0)=0.976 — the lower bound essentially touches zero. So the *only*
positive verdict (vs XLV) is fragile, and vanishes against the market itself. **Signal — WEAK.**

## Myth-check — it is LLY, not "the GLP-1 theme"

Single-name market model vs SPY (HAC-t on alpha):

| name | alpha vs SPY | HAC-t | β |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **LLY** | +26.58%/yr | **2.66** | 0.66 |
| **NVO** | +3.77%/yr | **0.35** | 0.63 |

The basket's entire alpha is **LLY**. NVO — *the company that actually makes Ozempic* — adds
**no** statistically distinguishable alpha (t = 0.35) and is **−69% from its peak**. The
"weight-loss-drug basket" is one drug-maker carrying a passenger. **Myth-check —
MISATTRIBUTED** (it's a single-name bet wearing a theme's clothes).

## Recency — the trade flipped *during* the boom it's named for

Split at 2023-01-01, when the GLP-1 mania took off:

| sub-period | basket CAGR | SPY CAGR | ann excess vs SPY | HAC-t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2018–2022 (before) | 29.9% | 11.1% | **+18.8%** | 1.93 |
| 2023–2026 (the mania) | 18.4% | 21.9% | **−3.5%** | −0.21 |

The excess was *positive before* the Ozempic story and **negative during it** — the sign
flips. By the verdict rubric a sign-flip across a justified split is the signature of a
**`MIXED`/regime-conditioned** effect, not a durable edge.

## Tradability — costs are a red herring; concentration is the killer

Mean one-way rebalancing turnover is **0.367%/day** of NAV, so costs barely move the needle:

| one-way cost | net ann excess vs XLV | HAC-t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | +15.14% | 2.01 |
| 5 bps | +15.09% | 2.01 |
| 10 bps | +15.04% | 2.00 |

The idea doesn't die to the spread — it dies to **concentration**: a **two-name** book (corr
0.40) with a **−49% drawdown**, whose whole thesis rides one product cycle and one company's
pipeline. That is beta to a story, not a harvestable, scalable edge. **Tradability — MIRAGE.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic one-factor panel (fixed seed) plants a *known* daily alpha per name; the
market-model engine must recover it (and its absence):

| name | planted alpha | recovered | HAC-t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| LLY | +25.2%/yr | +33.8%/yr | **4.33** |
| NVO | 0.0%/yr | −2.9%/yr | −0.39 |
| XLV | +5.0%/yr | +9.7%/yr | 1.21 |

The engine flags the planted edge (LLY, t=4.33) and correctly *fails to find* alpha where
none was planted (NVO, t=−0.39) — to Monte-Carlo error. A machinery proof, not market
evidence.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The basket's excess over SPY is HAC-t = 1.10 (fails ≥2); over XLV it is
  2.01 with a bootstrap CI [+0.2%, +29.3%] that grazes zero, and the market-model α vs SPY is
  t = 1.78. Add the recency/post-hoc selection (these two names are picked *because* they won)
  and the honest read is: the literature/headline says "alpha"; this tape can't certify it.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A two-name, −49%-drawdown bet on one product cycle. Costs are
  immaterial (≤0.1bp/yr); what's left is concentrated beta to a story, not a scalable edge.
- **Myth-check — MISATTRIBUTED.** The alpha is *all LLY* (t=2.66); NVO, the actual Ozempic
  maker, contributes none (t=0.35) and is −69% from peak — and the basket's excess turned
  **negative** during the very GLP-1 mania it is named for.
